prompt: A ladder leans against a wall. It touches the wall $5$ m up, and its foot sits $5$ m out from the wall. What angle does the ladder make with the ground, in degrees?
hint: You know the opposite side ($5$ up) and the adjacent side ($5$ out), so use tangent.

hints.text: You know the opposite side ($5$ up) and the adjacent side ($5$ out), so use tangent.
$\tan(\text{angle}) = \frac{5}{5} = 1$. Which angle has a tangent of $1$?

explanation: Opposite $= 5$ and adjacent $= 5$, so use TOA.
Inverse tangent turns the ratio back into an angle: the angle is $45^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spot the 45-45-90 triangle
steps: Both legs are $5$, so the triangle is isosceles.
The two non-right angles must be equal and add to $90^\circ$.
$90 \div 2 = 45$, so the ladder meets the ground at $45^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw and sanity-check
steps: Sketch it: the ladder goes up exactly as much as it goes out.
That slant is a perfect diagonal, halfway between flat and straight up.
